title: Stream Train Sends Six Players Livestreaming Through Cryptid Country
excerpt: Stream Train, Half Past Yellow's co-op horror game about livestreaming through cryptid country, is out on Steam and 35% off for 14 days.
content:
Max Wrighton, game director at Half Past Yellow, is sending players into the Uncanny Valley, a stretch of abandoned railroad crawling with cryptids, ghosts and angry forest spirits. Stream Train, the Copenhagen studio’s co-op survival horror game, launched on Steam on Friday, October 16, 2026. You and up to five friends ride an old steam train through it, and the whole trip is a livestream.

That framing is the motive behind everything in the game. Your squad isn’t trying to escape the woods so much as go viral in them.

A Virtual Chat Decides Whether You Eat

The setup is simple. Players customize their avatars, climb aboard, and follow the tracks past derelict buildings and strange creatures. They film all of it for a virtual audience that reacts in real time.

The chat is more than background noise. According to the press release, chatters issue challenges, make requests and send donations when you give them something worth watching. Those donations are “vital for making it through alive.”

So the arc of a run is a loop. You capture content, pull off pranks and keep the camera rolling. Chat pays you for it, and you spend that money on fuel and gear to push farther down the railway toward the next stop.

The studio sums up the golden rule of the Valley in one line: try not to make the monsters angry, “or at least film it when you do.”

Bad Decisions Are the Whole Point

Half Past Yellow leans hard into friend-group chaos. One of the listed features is literally called “Make Bad Decisions Together,” and the pitch says some encounters only turn dangerous once your friends get involved.

That tells you what kind of horror this is. The scares come from ghosts and cryptids, but the stories you walk away with will be about the teammate who poked the thing they were told not to poke.

Pricing and the Mixed Early Reviews

The launch discount is 35% off for 14 days. Steam currently lists Stream Train at $5.19, down from $7.99, as of October 17. The sale price won’t last, so check the store page before you buy.

Early reception is lukewarm. The Steam page shows “Mixed” user reviews across 45 reviews at the time of writing. That’s a small sample, and a cheap co-op game can swing a lot in its first weekend. Still, it’s worth reading a few reviews before you drag your whole crew aboard.

The studio says a playtest with more than 10,000 players came first. That test led to adjustments before launch, though the release doesn’t say what changed.

What Half Past Yellow Says Comes Next

Wrighton framed launch day as a starting point rather than a finish line. In the studio’s words:

“We are over the moon to let players explore the Uncanny Valley as of today. The launch is not the end for us as we are planning to make some quality of life improvement to the game as well as bringing more items, locations, and monsters over the next couple of months.” – Max Wrighton, Game Director, in a press release

More monsters and more locations would give the setup more room to grow. A loop built on filming scary things works better the more scary things there are to film.

Stream Train is on Steam for Windows, and the page lists English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Turkish, Russian and Brazilian Portuguese. The studio was founded in 2017 and is best known for Time on Frog Island, which won Best Debut and Best Kids Game at Spilprisen 2023. This is a very different kind of trip, and the Mixed reviews will be the first test of whether the new one lands.

The store page is at https://store.steampowered.com/app/4071650 if you want to check the price before the 14 days run out.
